description: I am a research strategist and UI designer driven by space exploration and human factors. I specialize in turning complex research into intuitive digital solutions for extreme environments. Joining us means building high-impact, story-driven technology. We are currently looking for teammates skilled in software development, data science, and hardware prototyping.
summary:
ARES OS (Autonomous Recovery and Equilibrium System) is an autonomous neuro-therapeutic operating system and behavioural health sanctuary built to Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions. On deep-space Mars missions, 40-minute communication delays make real-time psychological crisis support from Earth impossible. Grounded in NASA-STD-3001 Rev. C, NASA HRP Standard Measures, and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) radiation data, ARES OS passively fuses multi-modal telemetry—ECG, Heart Rate Variability (HRV), EEG spectra, and voice-pitch jitter—into a real-time Acute Distress Index (ADI). When elevated stress or insomnia is detected, our Therapeutic Matrix autonomously dims cabin lighting to 1800K amber phototherapy, activates 40 Hz vibroacoustics and 6 Hz Theta audio, launches AI Psychological First Aid (AI PFA) voice grounding, and projects VR Earth biomes with pre-buffered family videos. For acute psychosis emergencies, role-specific interfaces enforce a Level-4 Dual-Key Emergency Anti-Psychotic Protocol (EAP) for the Flight Commander and CMO, plus an Astronaut Emergency Override. ARES OS protects human minds from NASA's HERA analogues to Mars and isolated Earth outposts.

====================================================================

1. THE WHY, THE WHAT & THE HOW: WHAT ARES OS DOES & HOW IT WORKS

====================================================================

THE CHALLENGE WE ADDRESS (THE WHY):

Built for the challenge to "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions," ARES OS (Autonomous Recovery and Equilibrium System) solves a critical survival bottleneck on deep-space missions to the Moon and Mars. When astronauts travel toward Mars, radio signals take up to 20 minutes one-way (40 minutes round-trip) to reach Earth, making real-time psychological crisis intervention from ground flight surgeons impossible.

According to NASA's Human Research Program (HRP) "5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight" and "Risks of Human Spaceflight," crews endure extreme isolation, confinement, hostile closed environments, altered gravity, and space radiation. NASA's Integrated Medical Model (IMM) in NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 Revision C (Appendix E, Table E.2-1) identifies Late Insomnia as the #1 most frequent spaceflight medical event (13.85 occurrences per mission), followed by Space Motion Sickness (4.37/mission) and Spaceflight Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome (SANS, 2.08/mission). Furthermore, NASA's Astronaut Journals study (Experiment 01-E104, Stuster, 2010) proves a severe "Third Quarter Phenomenon" drop in emotional positivity and morale, while astronauts frequently withhold early psychological symptoms from ground flight surgeons due to fear of flight disqualification. In direct compliance with NASA-STD-3001 Vol. 1 Rev. C [V1 3004.q], ARES OS provides an autonomous, asynchronous electronic neuro-therapeutic sanctuary that detects distress passively and intervenes immediately onboard.

HOW ARES OS WORKS (THE WHAT & THE HOW):

Live at https://ares-os.ai.studio/, ARES OS v2.4 operates as a closed-loop neuro-therapeutic operating system featuring role-specific interfaces for Designated Crew Members (Patients), the Crew Medical Officer (CMO), and the Flight Commander across four integrated modules:

1. Biometrics & Waveforms Engine (Passive Multi-Modal Telemetry):

Instead of forcing fatigued astronauts to fill out intrusive questionnaires, ARES OS continuously analyses Lead-II ECG (87 BPM), depressed Heart Rate Variability (HRV: 53 ms), blood oxygen (SpO2: 98%), Delta/Theta/Alpha/Beta EEG brainwave power spectra, acoustic voice-pitch jitter (3.2%), and short-radius centrifuge telemetry (10 RPM / 0.22g). Using baselines from NASA HRP's International Standard Measures (AGBRESA 60-day study) and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) radiation-to-CNS monitoring principles, it computes a real-time Acute Distress Index (ADI = 0.59 Moderate).

2. Closed-Loop Therapeutic Matrix (Zero-Effort Environmental Reset):

When the ADI crosses nominal Permissible Outcome Limits, ARES OS autonomously triggers a multi-sensory countermeasure suite without requiring crew effort:

• Dynamic Circadian Phototherapy: Shifts cabin solid-state lighting from blue-enriched 6500K Wake Cyan to a blue-depleted 1800K Sleep Amber spectrum to stimulate natural melatonin synthesis and protect the 8.5-hour sleep window per NASA-STD-3001 [V1 6001].

• Acoustic & Somatosensory Therapy: Activates 40 Hz vibroacoustic bed resonance and 2–12 kPa deep-pressure seat stimulation alongside Web Audio-synthesised 6 Hz Theta binaural beats and Pacific Northwest rain soundscapes to mask 60 dB spacecraft air-recycler hum and relieve muscle rigidity.

3. AI PFA (Psychological First Aid) Protocol:

Powered by Google Gemini and grounded in NASA's Cognitive Behavioural Training framework (Moomaw, 2011), our asynchronous AI companion tracks voice-log sentiment using NASA's Net Positivity/Negativity (NPN) formula (Stuster, 2010) and guides real-time box breathing, sensory masking, and emotional grounding during 40-minute communication blackouts or solar-storm lockdowns.

4. VR Biophilia, Family Media Buffer & Level-4 Dual-Key Safety Protocols:

Projects 360-degree Earth forest, ocean, and rain biomes focused at optical infinity (relaxing ocular accommodation to mitigate SANS eye strain per [V1 3004.g]) while streaming pre-buffered family video messages to preserve oxytocin and soothe "Earth-out-of-view" grief. For high-consequence psychiatric emergencies such as acute psychosis or delirium (NASA-STD-3001 Table E.2-2, p. 85), ARES OS provides encrypted clinical logs, live triage, and a Level-4 High-Stress Dual-Key Authorisation Protocol for the Emergency Anti-Psychotic Protocol (EAP)—requiring joint cryptographic confirmation from both the Flight Commander and CMO per [V1 3004.k], [V1 3006] and the ISS 3.001 Medical Kit Checklist—while the Astronaut Emergency Override (Doomsday Protocol) unlocks autonomous life-saving care if both officers are incapacitated.

====================================================================

2. COMMUNITY INVOLVEMENT, BENEFITS, INTENDED IMPACT & CREATIVITY

====================================================================

HOW OUR PROJECT IS CREATIVE:

Traditional spaceflight behavioural health tools rely on self-reported surveys and delayed ground conferences that astronauts actively avoid when stressed. ARES OS pioneers a "Dark Cockpit" exception-based medical UI (inspired by NASA Astro UXDS and Orion MEDS standards) that bridges passive multi-modal telemetry with automated habitat hardware, Web Audio neuro-acoustics, AI voice grounding, and dual-key pharmacological safety governance in a single web platform.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT (SPACE & EARTH):

• Deep-Space & Analogue Validation Roadmap: Following NASA's HRP Analogue Framework (Vessey et al., 2020), ARES OS is ready for immediate ground validation in NASA's HERA (45-day isolation at Johnson Space Centre), DLR's :envihab, and NEK/SIRIUS analogues before scaling to Artemis Lunar Gateway and Mars transit habitats.

• Terrestrial Community Impact on Earth: Inspired by the Canadian Space Agency's framework ("Why Do We Conduct Science Experiments in Space?"), ARES OS directly translates spaceflight tele-psychiatry to isolated, confined, and extreme (ICE) environments on Earth—protecting Antarctic winter-over researchers, nuclear submarine crews, offshore oil rig workers, disaster first responders, and rural ICU telehealth patients lacking real-time psychiatric specialists.

FACTORS CONSIDERED (ENERGY, ACCESSIBILITY, USABILITY & COST):

• Energy & Bandwidth Efficiency: Engineered for power-constrained spacecraft and 40-minute communication blackouts; biometric signal fusion, Web Audio frequency generation (40 Hz / 6 Hz), and pre-buffered family media run locally with minimal wattage and zero dependency on live Earth bandwidth.

• Accessibility & Microgravity Usability: Designed around NASA-STD-3001 Volume 2 human-factors rules with high-contrast 4-state telemetry colour coding (Nominal, Caution, Warning, Critical), wide tremor-safe sliders for microgravity or anxious hands, shallow 4-tab navigation, and zero-click automated therapy activation so a panicking astronaut requires zero training.

• Cost & Hardware Agnosticism: Built as an open-source, lightweight web operating system that interfaces with commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) biometric wearables, smart LEDs, tactile transducers, and VR headsets at a fraction of custom avionics cost.

====================================================================

3. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, SOFTWARE & DATASETS USED

====================================================================

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE:

• Frontend & Core Architecture: HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript / JavaScript, React, and Lucide Icons.

• Audio & Signal Synthesis: Web Audio API (real-time oscillator synthesis for 6 Hz Theta binaural beats and 40 Hz vibroacoustic frequencies).

• AI, Voice & Prototyping Tools: Google AI Studio (https://ares-os.ai.studio/), Google Gemini API (AI PFA grounding & NPN sentiment engine), ElevenLabs API (human-emotional voiceover synthesis from our original script), Google Flow (concept visuals), and Canva (video editing and captioning).

• Target Hardware Ecosystem: Multi-modal wearable biosensors (Lead-II ECG, PPG/HRV, dry-electrode EEG headband, cabin microphone array), 1800K–6500K solid-state circadian LEDs, 40 Hz vibroacoustic bed transducers, and optical-infinity VR headset.

NASA & SPACE AGENCY PARTNER DATASETS INTEGRATED:

1. NASA HRP — 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight (https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/hazards/)

2. NASA HRP — Risks of Human Spaceflight (https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/risks/)

3. NASA HRP — Ongoing HRP Research in Space (https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/ongoing-hrp-research/)

4. Canadian Space Agency (CSA) — Monitoring Radiation for Astronaut Health (https://www.asc-csa.gc.ca/eng/news/articles/2026/2026-02-26-monitoring-radiation-astronaut-health.asp)

5. Canadian Space Agency (CSA) — Why Do We Conduct Science Experiments in Space? (https://www.asc-csa.gc.ca/eng/iss/science/why-do-we-conduct-science-experiments-in-space.asp)

6. NASA-STD-3001, Volume 1, Revision C (2023) — Crew Health Standards & Appendix E Integrated Medical Model (IMM) Risk Tables E.2-1 & E.2-2.

7. NASA HRP International Standard Measures (AGBRESA 60-Day Study, Clément et al., 2022) & Artificial Gravity Cognitive Dataset (Tays et al., 2022).

8. NASA Astronaut Journals Dataset (Experiment 01-E104, Stuster, 2010), NASA Spaceflight CBT Countermeasures (Moomaw, 2011), ISS 3.001 Medical Kit Checklist (NASA JSC), and NASA Open Data APIs (https://api.nasa.gov/).
